salient_findings: Severe macular changes with associated edema
key_facts: Vision loss in the right eye
Ophthalmoscopic examination revealed severe macular changes

raw.syndrome_frame: Persistent vision loss with macular changes and edema
salient_findings: Severe macular changes with associated edema
key_facts: Vision loss in the right eye
Ophthalmoscopic examination revealed severe macular changes

shortlist.label: Cystoid Macular Edema
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has severe macular changes with associated edema, consistent with CME

shortlist.label: Central Retinal Vein Occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, increasing risk of CRVO

shortlist.label: Branch Retinal Vein Occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, increasing risk of BRVO

shortlist.label: Age-Related Macular Degeneration
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is 63 years old, increasing risk of AMD

shortlist.label: Diabetic Macular Edema
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has vision loss and macular changes, although no explicit diabetes diagnosis

shortlist.label: Ischemic Optic Neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has history of multiple strokes, increasing risk of ION

shortlist.label: Epiretinal Membrane
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has severe macular changes, which can be associated with epiretinal membrane

shortlist.label: Hemiretinal Vein Occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, increasing risk of HRVO

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of vision loss, severe macular changes, and associated edema, along with the spectral-domain optical coherence tomography findings showing persistent central macular thickness and changes in macular edema, are consistent with Cystoid Macular Edema, especially given the reversible effect on CME as described in the figure.

rejected.label: Central Retinal Vein Occlusion
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of multiple strokes and vision loss, the primary issue described is macular edema, not a vein occlusion.

rejected.label: Branch Retinal Vein Occlusion
rejected.why: Similar to central retinal vein occlusion, the focus is on macular changes and edema rather than a specific vein occlusion.

rejected.label: Age-Related Macular Degeneration
rejected.why: The patient's age could suggest this, but the presence of edema and reversible changes points more towards a condition like Cystoid Macular Edema.

rejected.label: Diabetic Macular Edema
rejected.why: There is no mention of diabetes in the patient's history, making this less likely.

rejected.label: Ischemic Optic Neuropathy
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and findings are more related to macular changes than optic neuropathy.

rejected.label: Epiretinal Membrane
rejected.why: While this could cause vision problems, the specific findings of macular edema and its changes over time are more indicative of Cystoid Macular Edema.

rejected.label: Hemiretinal Vein Occlusion
rejected.why: Like other vein occlusions, this does not directly explain the macular edema and its reversible nature as described in the case.
